title: 2017 AMC 10B Problem 20
statement: The number \(21!\) \(=51{,}090{,}942{,}171{,}709{,}440{,}000\) has over \(60{,}000\) positive integer divisors. One of them is chosen at random. What is the probability that it is odd?

solutions.text:
The exponent of \(2\) in \(21!\) is \[\begin{aligned} &\left\lfloor\dfrac{21}{2}\right\rfloor+ \left\lfloor\dfrac{21}{4}\right\rfloor\\ &\quad{}+\left\lfloor\dfrac{21}{8}\right\rfloor+ \left\lfloor\dfrac{21}{16}\right\rfloor\\ &=10+5+2+1=18. \end{aligned}\] Thus \(21!=2^{18}d\) for some odd integer \(d.\)

For every divisor \(x\) of \(d,\) the divisors of \(21!\) with odd part \(x\) are \(x,2x,\ldots,2^{18}x.\) Exactly one of these \(19\) divisors is odd, so the probability is \(\dfrac1{19}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B .
hints: For each odd part of a divisor, only one exponent of \(2\) gives an odd divisor
